account:
Today there is an unusually large amount of bread being arranged by the innkeeper, builder and freight operator. They are the committee for an eighteen-hundred gathering in the town hall, scheduled to last until eighteen-thirty, with the secretary escorting me. The updated appointment book calls it civic hospitality and community gatherings and records my approval yesterday. The secretary says residents are welcome, with refreshments, deliveries and hall lighting on the agenda. I saw a lantern added in the hall yesterday, which may fit those preparations.

The baker reported an original order of 120 loaves baked yesterday. Payment for that order remains unverified, and the secretary says she has authorized no treasury payment. Separately, she reports that the baker confirmed the builder paid thirty-two planks for eighty additional loaves. I personally heard the builder twice ask to collect the remaining thirty-two loaves from his paid order. I have also seen the innkeeper carrying a sack of bread. This suggests substantial refreshments are being gathered and transported, but I do not know why so much bread is needed or where all of it is going.

Two townsfolk repeated reports of a bridge or port change discussed at the bakery, naming the baker and various committee members. Those reports are vague and may repeat the same underlying news; I have no direct confirmation of an actual transport proposal. My questions to the committee have not produced a direct explanation, and several were not heard by their intended recipients. I should not mistake that for deliberate evasion.

My best current explanation is preparation for this evening's public gathering, possibly involving some transport-related town business. It could also be a community occasion whose full purpose I have not yet learned. The committee seems to know more than I do, but I have no proof of wrongdoing or a secret plan. The secretary has been helpful about the schedule and payment distinctions. I want to clarify the original order's payer and the reported bridge or port changes while keeping my appointments: council letters at one, tea with the neighbour at three, office at sixteen-thirty, and the hall at eighteen. I have now reached home for lunch, later than scheduled.
